Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan: President of the United Arab Emirates from 1971 to 2004.
Who among these was born first?
Georges Dumézil (born 1898) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four was born earliest?

Stephen Gray (scientist) (born 1666) is the earliest of the four. Stephen Gray (December 1666 – February 1736) was an English dyer and astronomer who was the first to systematically experiment with electrical conduction.
Which one below was established earliest?
Lisp (programming language) (founded 1958) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is an astronomer?
Which of these four is a mathematician?
What is the atomic number of Silver?
Silver is a chemical element; it has symbol Ag (from Latin argentum 'silver') and atomic number 47.
What is the atomic number of Calcium?
Calcium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ca and atomic number 20.
In what year was Sam Altman born?
Sam Altman: Altman attended Stanford University for two years before he dropped out and co-founded Loopt, a smartphone geosocial networking service.
In what year was Bayes' theorem discovered?
Bayes' theorem: The theorem was developed in the 18th century by Bayes and independently by Pierre-Simon Laplace.
Genetics: Gregor Mendel. Genetics is the study of genes, genetic variation, and heredity in organisms.
Doxycycline: Pfizer. It is used to treat bacterial pneumonia, acne, chlamydia infections, Lyme disease, cholera, typhus, and syphilis, and is sometimes used to prevent malaria.
Which country is Bombardier Challenger 600 series from?
Bombardier Challenger 600 series: Canada. At the end of 1975, Canadair began funding the development of LearStar 600, and then bought the design for a wide-cabin business jet in April 1976.
Who is credited with discovering Hassium?
GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research
Hassium: GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research. Hassium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Hs and atomic number 108.
Who is credited with discovering HD 209458 b?
HD 209458 b: Michel Mayor. It is sometimes informally called Osiris.
Who is credited with discovering Osmium?
Osmium: Smithson Tennant. Osmium (from Ancient Greek ὀσμή (osmḗ) 'smell') is a chemical element; it has symbol Os and atomic number 76.
One of the very few semiaquatic vipers in the world, which venomous pit viper native to the southeastern United States is often found coiled near slow-moving lakes, streams, and marshes?
Agkistrodon piscivorus is a species of venomous snake, a pit viper in the subfamily Crotalinae of the family Viperidae.

With more than 140 species spread across 16 genera in oceans worldwide, these small forage fish are usually classified as oily fish, and a few South American species live only in fresh water — name this fish?
Anchovy are small, common forage fish of the family Engraulidae.
Excavated in Argentina starting in 1989 under paleontologist José Bonaparte, this Late Cretaceous titanosaur weighed as much as 80 tons — which genus of giant sauropod?
Argentinosaurus (meaning "lizard from Argentina") is a genus of giant sauropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period in what is now Argentina.

Developed in Great Britain around the 1830s from breeds like the Talbot Hound, this scent hound — smaller than the similar-looking foxhound — was originally bred to hunt rabbits and hares — name the breed?
Beagle is a British breed of scent hound, similar in appearance to the much larger foxhound.
This insect order contains both cockroaches and termites — the latter now classified as a specialized, social lineage within the former group — what order is it?
Blattodea is an order of insects that contains cockroaches and termites.

More muscular and aggressive than the females of the species, this uncastrated adult male of Bos taurus has long symbolized power in religious sacrifice and features prominently in ranching and blood sports — which term describes him?
Bull is an intact (i.e., not castrated) adult male of the species Bos taurus (cattle).
This Mexican business magnate was ranked the richest person in the world by Forbes from 2010 to 2013, building his fortune through a sprawling conglomerate called Grupo Carso. Who is he?
Carlos Slim (born 28 January 1940) is a Mexican business oligarch, investor and philanthropist.
The principal sterol of all animals, it concentrates in the brain and spinal cord and is essential to every cell membrane — yet too much in the blood spells trouble. What is it?
Cholesterol is the principal sterol of all animals, distributed in body tissues, especially the brain and spinal cord, and in animal fats and oils.
This legless, non-venomous lizard native to Europe is often mistaken for a snake despite having smooth, non-overlapping scales and semi-fossorial burrowing habits — what is it called?
Common slow worm (Anguis fragilis) is a non-venomous species of legless lizard native to Europe.
Grown from tubers and known by the folk name 'sowbread,' this Primulaceae genus features flowers with distinctively upswept petals — which plant genus?
Cyclamen is a genus of 25 species of perennial flowering plants in the family Primulaceae.

Bred in the early twentieth century in Córdoba, Argentina, for hunting big game like wild boar and pumas, this large mastiff-type dog breed traces its ancestry partly to a now-extinct fighting dog — name the breed?
Dogo Argentino (plural Dogos Argentinos) is an Argentine breed of large dog of mastiff type.
Born to a mathematician father in Erlangen, this pioneering algebraist proved theorems connecting symmetry to conservation laws in physics — who is she?
Emmy Noether (23 March 1882 - 14 April 1935) was a German mathematician who made many important contributions to abstract algebra.
Despite its name, this highly sociable oceanic dolphin earned its label from a skull resembling the orca's — it can reach 20 feet and even forms mixed pods with bottlenose dolphins. What is it?
False killer whale (Pseudorca crassidens) is a species of oceanic dolphin that is the only extant representative of the genus Pseudorca.

This American mechanical engineer and pioneering management consultant wrote a 1909 book that Academy of Management fellows later voted the most influential management book of the entire 20th century — who was he?
Frederick Winslow Taylor (March 20, 1856 - March 21, 1915) was an American mechanical engineer.
This ancient metabolic pathway breaks glucose down into pyruvate through ten enzyme-catalyzed reactions in a cell's cytosol, generating ATP along the way. What process is it?
Glycolysis is the metabolic pathway that converts glucose (C6H12O6) into pyruvate and, in most organisms, occurs in the liquid part of cells (the cytosol).
About the size of a closed fist and tucked between the lungs, this four-chambered muscular organ pumps blood throughout the body — name it?
Heart is a muscular organ found in humans and other animals.
A colourless, ammonia-scented liquid with formula N2H4, this hazardous compound foams polymers, inflates airbags, and serves as a storable spacecraft propellant. What is it?
Hydrazine is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula N2H4.
Serving as the continuous analog of a summation, this fundamental calculus operation is used to compute areas, volumes, and displacement from velocity — name the mathematical concept?
Integral is the continuous analog of a sum, and is used to calculate areas, volumes, and their generalizations.
The youngest division chief in GM history, this engineer shepherded the Pontiac GTO before founding the company behind a famously gull-winged car — who was he?
John DeLorean (d-; January 6, 1925 - March 19, 2005) was an American engineer, inventor, and executive in the U.S.
Named after a 19th-century Russian neuropsychiatrist, which memory disorder features confabulation and amnesia from vitamin B1 deficiency, often following an episode of Wernicke encephalopathy?
Korsakoff syndrome (KS) is a disorder of the central nervous system characterized by amnesia, deficits in explicit memory, and confabulation.
One of only five people to win multiple Nobel Prizes, this American chemist and peace activist is the sole person to have received two unshared Nobels — one in Chemistry, one for Peace. Who is he?
Linus Pauling (February 28, 1901 - August 19, 1994) was an American chemist and peace activist.

This colorless, highly water-soluble inorganic salt forms hydrates holding up to 12 water molecules per unit, and its anhydrous form is industry's main source for producing a lightweight, silvery-white structural metal — which compound is it?
Magnesium chloride is an inorganic compound with the formula MgCl2.
First made in 1955 by bombarding einsteinium with alpha particles, this synthetic element 101 is named for the father of the periodic table — what is it?
Mendelevium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Md (formerly Mv) and atomic number 101.

Caused by a poxvirus spread through direct contact, this viral skin infection produces small raised pink lesions with a distinctive dimple in the center, usually clearing on its own within a year — name the condition?
Molluscum contagiosum (MC), sometimes called water warts, is a viral infection of the skin that results in small raised pink lesions with a dimple in the center.

Nicknamed for its terrifying rate of tissue destruction, this fast-spreading bacterial infection doesn't actually consume flesh — the bacteria instead release toxins that destroy it — what is this disease called?
Necrotizing fasciitis (NF), also known as flesh-eating disease or flesh-eating bacteria, is an infection that kills the body's soft tissue.

Encompassing 24 genera from baboons to colobus to langurs, this is the largest primate family, having diverged from a separate primate lineage 45 to 55 million years ago before apes split off from it too — which family?
Old World monkey are primates in the family Cercopithecidae.
Making up the order Psittaciformes, these birds are known for a strong curved beak, upright stance, and clawed feet, with a third of all species threatened by extinction — name the group?
Parrot (order Psittaciformes), also known as psittacines from the name of the type genus Psittacus, are birds with a strong curved beak, upright stance, and clawed feet.
One of nine essential amino acids we must eat rather than make ourselves, it's found in mammals' milk and acts as a direct precursor to the neuromodulator phenethylamine — which molecule is it?
Phenylalanine (symbol Phe or F) is an -amino acid with the formula C9H11NO2.

This natural process transfers pollen from a flower's anther to its stigma, enabling fertilization and seed production, carried out by everything from bees and bats to wind and water — what process is it?
Pollination is the transfer of pollen from an anther of a plant to the stigma of a plant, later enabling fertilisation and the production of seeds.

This psychiatric state describes an inability to distinguish reality from delusion, marked by symptoms like hallucinations and disorganized thinking, and can stem from conditions like schizophrenia or bipolar disorder — name the state?
Psychosis is the inability to distinguish what is or is not real.
This inflammatory disease typically develops two to four weeks after a streptococcal throat infection and can damage the heart valves in about half of cases — what is it?
Rheumatic fever (RF) is an inflammatory disease that can involve the heart, joints, skin, and brain.
After dropping out of Stanford and co-founding a startup later sold for over $40 million, this entrepreneur led Y Combinator before taking the helm of a leading AI company — who is he?
Sam Altman (born April 22, 1985) is an American entrepreneur and investor who has been the chief executive officer (CEO) of the artificial intelligence company OpenAI since 2019.
The smallest of Japan's six native dog breeds, this small, alert hunting dog's name literally translates to 'brushwood dog,' reflecting its original job of flushing game — which breed?
Shiba Inu (Japanese) is a breed of hunting dog from Japan.

Meaning 'pore bearer' in Greek, this phylum of sessile, filter-feeding marine invertebrates has tube-like bodies of jelly-like material sandwiched between thin cell layers, letting water circulate through countless pores — name the animal group?
Sponge are primarily marine invertebrates of the animal phylum Porifera (meaning 'pore bearer').

This amniote lineage — one of just two major branches alongside the reptile-and-bird clade — is marked by a single temporal opening behind the eye and gave rise to every mammal alive today — name the group?
Synapsida is a diverse group of tetrapod vertebrates that includes all mammals and their extinct relatives.
This genus of coniferous evergreen in the cypress family includes five species — two native to North America, three to eastern Asia — and is sister to the genus Thujopsis. Name the genus?
Thuja is a genus of coniferous tree or shrub in the Cupressaceae (cypress family).
The two major groups of these reptiles, side-necked and hidden-necked, differ in how they pull in the head — and they breathe air despite many living in water. What animal?
Turtle (order Testudines) are reptiles characterized by a special shell developed mainly from their ribs, as well as keratinized toothless beak.

This trailing vine of the gourd family bears a fruit that's botanically a 'pepo' — a hard-rinded berry with no internal divisions — and comes in more than 1,000 varieties, even seedless ones. What is it?
Watermelon (Citrullus lanatus) is a species of flowering plant in the family Cucurbitaceae, that has a large, edible fruit.
Adding or subtracting this number leaves any other number unchanged. In mathematical terms it is the additive what, of the integers and the reals?

0 is a number representing an empty quantity. Adding or subtracting 0 to any number leaves that number unchanged; in mathematical terminology 0 is the additive identity of the integers, rational numbers, real numbers and complex numbers.
Considered sacred by Hindus and Buddhists, this tree native to the Indian subcontinent is also known as bael and is the sole member of its genus — which species?
Aegle marmelos: Species of tree, considered sacred by Hindus. It is present in India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, and Nepal as a naturalized species.
With the general formula CnH2n+2 and every carbon-carbon bond single, methane is the simplest example of this class of hydrocarbons — what's it called?
Alkane: Type of saturated hydrocarbon compound.
This group of diseases occurs when misfolded proteins accumulate in body tissue, causing fatigue, swelling, and shortness of breath among roughly 36 distinct protein-driven types — what is it?
Amyloidosis: Metabolic disease involving abnormal deposited amyloid proteins.
Usually symptomless until it ruptures — causing sudden, severe abdominal or lower-back pain — this dangerous enlargement of the body's main artery is most common in the abdomen — what condition?
Aortic aneurysm: Excessive enlargement of the human aorta.
Born from acetylsalicylic acid, this everyday drug cools fevers within about 30 minutes and is taken long-term to fend off heart attacks and strokes by quieting platelets — what is it?
One of the first grains ever domesticated, around 9000 BC in the Fertile Crescent, this cereal now ranks fourth in world production — and 70% of it goes to feeding animals — what is it?
Barley: Cereal grain. Barley (Hordeum vulgare), a member of the grass family, is a major cereal grain grown in temperate climates globally.
Split into structural biology, enzymology, and metabolism, this scientific field studies the chemical processes that occur within living organisms — which field?

Biochemistry: Study of chemical processes of living organisms. Biochemistry, or biological chemistry (distinct from chemical biology), is the study of chemical processes within and relating to living organisms.

Bred in South Africa as a family guard dog, this large mastiff-type breed has a short coat and heavy bone structure, and is recognized by that country's kennel union but not the international federation — what breed is it?
Boerboel: South African breed of dog. The Boerboel (pronounced [ˈbuːrbul]) is a South African breed of large dog of mastiff type, used as a family guard dog.
An intact, more muscular and aggressive adult male of the cattle species, this animal has long been a sacrificial symbol in many religions and stars in famous arena sports. What is it?
Bull: Adult male cattle. A bull is an intact (i.e., not castrated) adult male of the species Bos taurus (cattle).
Also known as hemp when grown for fiber rather than its psychoactive use, this Asian-native plant genus includes up to three disputed species — which plant?
Also known as an Ovcharka, this large livestock-guardian breed was developed in the Soviet Union around 1920 from mountain and steppe animals of the Caucasus region — which breed?
Caucasian Shepherd Dog: Russian breed of livestock guardian dog. It was bred in the Soviet Union from about 1920 from dogs of the Caucasus Mountains and the steppe regions of Southern Russia.
Her famous experiment proved parity is not conserved — earning Lee and Yang the 1957 Nobel while she received the inaugural Wolf Prize in Physics instead. Which Manhattan Project physicist was she?
This genus of anaerobic, Gram-positive bacteria found in soil and animal intestines includes the microbes responsible for both botulism and tetanus — which genus?
Clostridium: Genus of bacteria. Species of Clostridium inhabit soils and the intestinal tracts of animals, including humans.
Named from ancient Greek for 'footless' after being mistaken for a legless swallow, this bird's closest relatives are actually hummingbirds — and it almost never touches the ground. Which bird?
Common swift: Species of bird. The resemblances between the groups are due to convergent evolution, reflecting similar contextual development.
Unknown in the wild, this cultivated autumn-flowering plant has had its dried stigmas prized as the world's priciest spice for over 3,500 years — what is its scientific name?
Crocus sativus: Species of flowering plant. Crocus sativus, commonly known as saffron crocus or autumn crocus, is a species of flowering plant in the iris family Iridaceae.
Introduced in 1984, this turboprop regional airliner series was developed from an earlier company model and later gained 'Quiet' variants with active noise-cancellation — which aircraft family?

De Havilland Canada Dash 8: Canadian turboprop airliner. The De Havilland Canada DHC-8, commonly known as the Dash 8, is a series of turboprop-powered regional airliners, introduced by de Havilland Canada (DHC) in 1984.

The largest collection of fossils from this extinct Ice Age canine came from the La Brea Tar Pits in Los Angeles, though it roamed from South American savanna to North American forested mountains — what animal was it?
Dire wolf: Extinct species of canine mammal.
This condition involves involuntarily repeating words or sounds spoken by someone else, and is commonly seen in autism, ADHD, and Tourette syndrome. What is it called?

This is the process of creating economic value by spotting and commercializing opportunities — typically demanding considerable initiative and bearing real risk in exchange for most of the reward. What's the term?
Entrepreneurship: Taking financial risks in the hope of profit.
Also known by the scientific name Gyps fulvus, this large Old World bird of prey belongs to the family Accipitridae — which species is it?
Eurasian griffon vulture: Species of bird. It is also known as the Eurasian griffon or griffon vulture, although the latter term is sometimes used for the genus Gyps as a whole.
This centuries-old number theory statement claims there are no positive whole-number solutions to a^n + b^n = c^n whenever the exponent exceeds two — what's it called?
Fermat's Last Theorem: 17th-century conjecture proved by Andrew Wiles in 1994.
This American chemical engineer at Caltech won the 2018 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for pioneering 'directed evolution' to engineer enzymes — and later joined Alphabet's board — who is it?
Frances Arnold: American chemist and academic (born 1956)
Once Mexico's top law-enforcement official as secretary of public security, this man was convicted in a Brooklyn courtroom in 2023 for taking millions in bribes from the Sinaloa Cartel — who is he?
Genaro García Luna: Mexican politician and convicted felon (born 1968)
With the symbol Au and atomic number 79, this soft, dense element is so unreactive that only platinum sits below it — and it often turns up as native nuggets in riverbeds. What is it?
Gold: Chemical element with atomic number 79 (Au). Chemically, gold is a transition metal, a group 11 element, and one of the noble metals.

Named from Greek words meaning 'naked seed,' this group of woody plants — including conifers, cycads, and ginkgos — lacks the protective covering that encloses a flowering plant's seeds. What is it called?
Gymnosperm: Clade of non-flowering, naked-seeded vascular plants.

Often triggered by a preceding throat infection, this childhood autoimmune disease causes raised skin bruising, joint pain, and sometimes kidney trouble from IgA immune-complex deposits — what is it called?
Henoch–Schönlein purpura: Autoimmune vascular inflammatory disease.
Defined today as exactly 3,600 seconds, this unit of time was originally a variable measure equal to one-twelfth of the night or day in the ancient Near East — which unit?
Hour: Unit of time equal to 60 minutes.

Once diagnosed almost exclusively in women during the 19th century and studied intensely by Sigmund Freud and Jean-Martin Charcot, this term for 'ungovernable emotional excess' is no longer accepted as a medical diagnosis. What is it called?
Hysteria: Excess, ungovernable emotion. Hysteria is a term used to mean ungovernable emotional excess and can refer to a temporary state of mind or emotion.
This condition restricts blood flow to tissue, starving cells of oxygen and nutrients due to causes like thrombosis or embolism — what's it called?
Ischemia: Restriction in blood supply to tissues.
As Grand Pensionary of Holland during the Dutch Golden Age, this statesman dominated politics from 1650 until the 'Disaster Year' of 1672 — who was he?
This Hungarian-American biochemist spent years fighting skepticism over messenger RNA before her groundwork made mRNA vaccines possible, earning a shared 2023 Nobel Prize — who is she?
At Bologna in the 1700s she became the first woman to hold a science doctorate and the first salaried female university teacher — depicted as the goddess Minerva herself; who was she?
Laura Bassi: Italian physicist and academic (1711–1778)
Nearly always affecting women, this incurable condition causes fat buildup in both legs that's resistant to typical weight loss and often mistaken for other circulatory disorders — what is it?
Lipedema: Condition involving excessive deposition of fat in the legs.
Native to China, Japan, Korea and Nepal and blooming in late summer after heavy rainfall, this plant's alternate names include the hurricane lily and the corpse flower — what is it?
Lycoris radiata: Species of plant. It is originally from China, Japan, Korea and Nepal and spread from there to the United States and elsewhere.

Often making people tall and thin with long fingers and very flexible joints, this connective-tissue disorder carries serious risks to the heart and aorta — caused by a mutation in the FBN1 fibrillin gene — which condition?
Marfan syndrome: Genetic disorder involving connective tissue.

Fever, a fierce headache, neck stiffness, and a telltale rash that doesn't fade when a glass is rolled over it can signal this inflammation of the membranes around the brain and spinal cord — what is it?

Meningitis: Inflammation of membranes around the brain. Meningitis (pl. meningitides) is acute or chronic inflammation of the protective membranes covering the brain and spinal cord, collectively called the meninges.

Soviet pilots called it the "Balalaika" because its planform looked like the stringed instrument, while Poles dubbed it "Ołówek" — the pencil — for its slender fuselage; which most-produced supersonic jet in history earned all those nicknames?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-21: 1956 Soviet fighter aircraft family.
Nicknamed noni, this pungent-smelling fruit tree in the coffee family was spread across the Pacific by Polynesian sailors and is now used mainly in traditional medicine and juices — which plant?
Morinda citrifolia: Species of plant. It is commonly known as noni or Indian mulberry, among many other names.
Originating near the Beijing region and used throughout East Asian cooking, this Brassica rapa vegetable spread to Europe, the Americas, and Australia during the 20th century — which vegetable is it?
Napa cabbage: Subspecies of flowering plant.
Humphry Davy coined this colorless gas's cheerful nickname for the euphoria it brings, and it still earns a spot on the WHO's Essential Medicines list for dentistry and surgery. What is it?
Nitrous oxide: Colourless non-flammable greenhouse gas.
This biological process turns a primary oocyte into an egg cell capable of developing once fertilized, beginning during embryonic development — what is it called?
Oogenesis: Egg cell production process. Oogenesis or ovogenesis is the differentiation of the ovum (egg cell) into a cell competent to further develop when fertilized.
Sold under the brand name Protonix, this proton-pump inhibitor treats ulcers and acid reflux but can, with long-term use, cause vitamin B12 deficiency and low magnesium — what is this drug?

This term for 'parts in each thousand' is symbolized by ‰ — a percent sign with an extra zero — and sits right next to the percent sign in Unicode's General Punctuation block — what is this unit called?
Per mille: Unit for parts per thousand. The associated symbol is ‰, similar to a per cent sign % but with an extra zero in the divisor.
This branch of biology studies how organs, cells, and biomolecules carry out their functions, and gives its name, alongside medicine, to a Nobel Prize category — which field?
Physiology: Science regarding functions in organisms or living systems.
First domesticated some 5,000 years ago on the Iranian plateau, this fruit-bearing shrub reached California in 1769 via Spanish settlers — which fruit?
Pomegranate: Fruit-bearing deciduous shrub. Pomegranate was first domesticated by ancient Iranians in the Iranian plateau and nearby regions about 5,000 years ago.
This thorny European shrub's tart fruit gives sloe gin its name in Britain, while its wood becomes the classic Irish walking stick — what is it?
Prunus spinosa: Species of flowering plant in the rose family.
Domesticated in Asia, this crunchy root vegetable in the mustard family owes its peppery bite to compounds like glucosinolate — what vegetable is it?
Radish: Root vegetable of the Brassicaceae family. The radish (Raphanus sativus or Raphanus raphanistrum subsp. sativus) is a flowering plant in the mustard family, Brassicaceae.

Grown for its fleshy, edible stalks since before the 18th century in Europe and Scandinavia, this plant's broad triangular leaves are actually poisonous due to their high oxalic acid content. What is it?
Rhubarb: Species of herbaceous perennial plant with fleshy, sour edible stalks.
First identified in November 2002 and traced through civets to horseshoe bats in Yunnan, this viral respiratory disease had an 11% fatality rate before its outbreak ended in 2003 — which disease?
Sitting near the center of the Milky Way between Libra and Sagittarius, this zodiac constellation's recognition predates ancient Greek culture — which constellation?
Scorpius: Zodiac constellation in the southern celestial hemisphere.
In this inherited blood disorder, faulty haemoglobin warps red cells into a rigid crescent shape that can't bend through capillaries, causing painful blockages — what is it?
Also known as milo, jowar, or Guinea corn, this grass — domesticated in Sudan and now grown worldwide — ranks as the fifth most important cereal crop on Earth — which grain?
Sorghum: Species of grain. It is typically an annual, but some cultivars are perennial.

These long-legged wading birds communicate by clattering their bills rather than calling, favor drier habitats than their heron cousins, and are collectively known as a 'muster' or a 'phalanx' — which birds?
Sold under the brand name Cialis, this erectile dysfunction medication can remain effective for up to 36 hours after a single dose — which drug?
Tadalafil: Medication used to treat erectile dysfunction.
The principal bitter alkaloid of the cacao plant, this caffeine cousin is found in chocolate, tea, and the kola nut, and works by blocking adenosine receptors. What is it?
Theobromine: Bitter alkaloid of the cacao plant. Theobromine, also known as xantheose, is the principal alkaloid of Theobroma cacao (cacao plant).
Caused by bacteria producing acid that breaks down enamel, dentin, and cementum, this common condition can turn dental cavities anywhere from yellow to black — what is it?
Tooth decay: Deformation of teeth due to acids produced by bacteria.

This orally contracted disease, caused by Salmonella Typhi bacteria, typically begins six to 30 days after exposure with a gradual high fever, weakness, and abdominal pain. Severe cases may produce distinctive rose-colored skin spots. What is this illness?

Typhoid fever: Disease caused by the bacteria Salmonella Typhi. Typhoid fever, also known as typhoid, is an orally contracted disease caused by Salmonella enterica serotype Typhi bacteria, also called Salmonella Typhi.
Posthumously awarded the Padma Vibhushan in 1972, this physicist and astronomer is regarded as the father of his country's space program — who is he?

Vikram Sarabhai: Indian physicist and astronomer. Often regarded as the "Father of Indian space program", Sarabhai was honored with Padma Bhushan in 1966 and the Padma Vibhushan (posthumously) in 1972.
Known also as the gnu, this African antelope comes in black and blue varieties whose lineages split roughly a million years ago — which animal?
Wildebeest: Genus of antelope. Wildebeest (WIL-di-beest;, VIL-,), also called gnu (NOO or, NEW), are antelopes of the genus Connochaetes and native to Eastern and Southern Africa.
Released from prison in June 2025, this Turkish politician resumed leading the nationalist Victory Party after previously serving as deputy leader of the MHP — who is he?
The symbol for radon is Rn. Radon is a chemical element; it has symbol Rn and atomic number 86.
